summary:
H.R. 7305, the “Energy Threat Analysis Center Act of 2026,” amends section 40125(c) of the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, codified at 42 U.S.C. 18724(c), governing the Department of Energy’s Energy Sector Operational Support for Cyberresilience Program. The bill reauthorizes the program by amending the redesignated authorization provision to replace fiscal years “2022 through 2026” with “2027 through 2031,” without specifying in the bill text any change to authorized funding levels.

Section 2 revises the program’s statutory purposes in section 40125(c)(1). It redesignates existing subparagraphs (A) through (E) as (B) through (F), inserts a new subparagraph (A), and strikes the redesignated subparagraph (F). The new purpose is to strengthen collective defense, response, and resilience of the United States energy sector by enhancing government-sector collaboration to analyze threats and deny, disrupt, and mitigate operational impacts to energy systems; exchanging classified and unclassified information; conducting collective analysis of potential and realized threats; providing mitigation recommendations benefiting the broader energy sector; establishing technical infrastructure for advanced analytics, experimentation, analysis, discovery, alerts, and collaboration involving intelligence-driven and intelligence-informed technical data, threat information, actionable insights, and threat mitigation; advancing collective understanding of national security risks and vulnerabilities associated with the energy sector; and increasing sector understanding of threat actor tactics, techniques, procedures, indicators of compromise, capabilities, and activities.

The bill redesignates existing paragraph (2) as paragraph (7) and inserts new paragraphs (2) through (6). New paragraph (2) authorizes, but does not require, the Secretary of Energy to carry out program activities through an Energy Threat Analysis Center, which may be established at one or more physical locations. New paragraph (3) provides that assistance or information furnished under the program is at the Secretary’s sole and unreviewable discretion and creates no substantive or procedural right or benefit for any other governmental or private entity. New paragraph (4) excludes the program from treatment as an advisory committee under chapter 10 of title 5, United States Code. New paragraph (5) exempts information shared by or with the Federal Government or a State, Tribal, or local government under the program from disclosure under 5 U.S.C. 552 and analogous State, Tribal, or local disclosure laws, and requires withholding without discretion under 5 U.S.C. 552(b)(3)(B). New paragraph (6) grants additional transaction authority to enter into contracts, cooperative agreements, grants, and other transactions, and authorizes pre-approved national security contracting mechanisms, model partnership agreements, and expedited review procedures. The bill contains no separate effective-date provision.
